advances: Proves a local ambient-halfspace transfer inequality from a barycentric volume-root parameter, and a pointwise centroid-depth certificate from the excess weights of any positive convex majorant of the integer-fiber volume roots. The same finite bad-set separation argument gives the requested comparison bound \(h_C((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))\ge\beta\tau(\mathbf j)\), its affine-root and log-affine cases, explicit stability under logarithmic error, and an aggregate majorant-error bound. These conclusions use the actual fibers and require no affine centroid map or common fiber shape. They establish the desired scale under the stated profile hypotheses; they do not establish a uniform approximation hypothesis for arbitrary convex bodies.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None beyond the declared accepted predecessors. The non-elementary inputs used above are the finite weighted lattice centerpoint construction and Grünbaum inequality in \(\texttt{bb2b5f9519ae23e8}\), and the compact-set Brunn-Minkowski input in \(\texttt{c13409b4041cc35d}\); their required forms and applicability are specified in the proof. The unverified local starting passages were `.math-prover/source_archives/2026-09-07/full-weak-oertel.txt` lines 20-151, `parity-comparison.txt` lines 570-712, and `logarithmic-loss.txt` lines 2317-2444. Their new transfer, majorant, and comparison claims are proved in this packet rather than assumed.
proof:
Compactness of the base projection of \(C\) implies that only finitely many integer fibers are nonempty. Thus \(D_+\) is finite and \(\mu_C(H)=\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{\mathbf z}\cap H_{\mathbf z})\). Each \(C_{\mathbf z}\) for \(\mathbf z\in D_+\) is a full-dimensional compact convex subset of \(\mathbb R^d\), and its centroid belongs to it.

We first check positivity at integer points in convex hulls of positive fibers. Suppose \(\mathbf j=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i\mathbf z_i\), where \(\mathbf z_i\in D_+\), \(\lambda_i>0\), and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\). Choose \(\mathbf x_i\in C_{\mathbf z_i}\) for \(i\ge2\). Convexity gives \(\lambda_1 C_{\mathbf z_1}+\sum_{i=2}^k\lambda_i\mathbf x_i\subseteq C_{\mathbf j}\), so \(w_{\mathbf j}\ge\lambda_1^d w_{\mathbf z_1}>0\). For \(k=1\) the same conclusion is immediate. Consequently \(\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{conv}(D_+)=D_+\); in particular every target \(\mathbf j\) used in (1) has a positive-volume fiber.

We use two inputs established in accepted fact \(\texttt{bb2b5f9519ae23e8}\). First, the finite-measure lattice centerpoint construction in its proof applies to any nonempty finite \(E_0\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) and any positive weights \(t_{\mathbf z}\) on \(E_0\): it returns \(\mathbf j\in\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{conv}(E_0)\) for which every proper closed base halfspace \(Q\ni\mathbf j\) satisfies \(\sum_{\mathbf z\in E_0\cap Q}t_{\mathbf z}\ge2^{-n}\sum_{\mathbf z\in E_0}t_{\mathbf z}\). The construction uses only the finite positive weights, so they need not be actual fiber volumes. Its claim that the selected point has a positive actual fiber follows here from the preceding paragraph whenever \(E_0\subseteq D_+\). Second, the Grünbaum input stated there gives \(\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{\mathbf j}\cap L)\ge\gamma_dw_{\mathbf j}\) for every proper closed fiber halfspace \(L\) containing \(\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}\).

The geometric input from accepted fact \(\texttt{c13409b4041cc35d}\) is its compact-fiber Brunn-Minkowski interpolation and its treatment of nonvertical complementary caps. We record the precise interpolation we use. If \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) is compact and convex, its fibers \(K_{\mathbf z_i}\) are nonempty, and \(\mathbf j=\sum_i\lambda_i\mathbf z_i\) with positive coefficients summing to one, then

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_i\lambda_i K_{\mathbf z_i}&\subseteq K_{\mathbf j},\\
\operatorname{vol}_d(K_{\mathbf j})^{1/d}
&\ge\sum_i\lambda_i\operatorname{vol}_d(K_{\mathbf z_i})^{1/d}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

The inclusion follows by taking convex combinations of points of \(K\). Repeated application of the nonempty compact-set Brunn-Minkowski inequality recorded in that accepted fact gives the volume inequality. All the Minkowski sums here are compact, and the inequality allows zero-volume fibers. We apply (4) only to \(K=C\) or \(K=C\cap H^-\), with explicitly nonempty source fibers. In particular, no concavity of a zero extension outside the projection of a cap body is asserted.

We also spell out the finite separation step. If a finite \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) has \(\mathbf j\notin\operatorname{conv}(B)\), then a proper closed base halfspace through \(\mathbf j\) avoids \(B\). When \(B\ne\varnothing\), choose \(\mathbf z_0\in\operatorname{conv}(B)\) minimizing its distance to \(\mathbf j\), and put \(\mathbf v_0=\mathbf j-\mathbf z_0\ne0\). For \(\mathbf z\in\operatorname{conv}(B)\), minimizing the squared distance along \(\mathbf z_0+t(\mathbf z-\mathbf z_0)\), \(0\le t\le1\), yields \(\langle\mathbf v_0,\mathbf z-\mathbf z_0\rangle\le0\). Hence \(\langle\mathbf v_0,\mathbf z-\mathbf j\rangle\le-\|\mathbf v_0\|^2<0\), so \(Q=\{\mathbf z:\langle\mathbf v_0,\mathbf z-\mathbf j\rangle\ge0\}\) is the required halfspace. When \(B=\varnothing\), any proper closed halfspace through \(\mathbf j\) works. This is the same finite separation used in accepted fact \(\texttt{c13409b4041cc35d}\), with its hypotheses checked directly.

For the parameter in (1), the feasible barycentric coefficients form a nonempty compact subset of the finite-dimensional simplex. The objective is continuous, so it attains a minimum. Since \(\sum_{\mathbf z\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf z}w_{\mathbf z}^{1/d}\ge\min_{\mathbf z\in E}w_{\mathbf z}^{1/d}>0\), the minimum is positive. Applying (4) with \(K=C\) to any feasible representation gives \((\sum_{\mathbf z\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf z}w_{\mathbf z}^{1/d})^d\le w_{\mathbf j}\). Thus \(0<\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)\le1\), as asserted.

Fix an arbitrary proper closed ambient halfspace \(H=\{(\mathbf z,\mathbf x):\langle\mathbf u,\mathbf z\rangle+\langle\mathbf v,\mathbf x\rangle\ge t\}\), where \((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\ne(\mathbf0,\mathbf0)\). If \(\mathbf v=\mathbf0\), write \(Q_H=\{\mathbf z:\langle\mathbf u,\mathbf z\rangle\ge t\}\). If \(\mathbf j\notin Q_H\), then \(p_{\mathbf j}(H)=0\), and the positive part in (1) is zero because \(\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)\le1\). If \(\mathbf j\in Q_H\), then \(p_{\mathbf j}(H)=1\) and \(\mu_C(H)\ge\sum_{\mathbf z\in E\cap Q_H}w_{\mathbf z}\ge\tau_E(\mathbf j)\). This includes \(\mathbf j\in\partial Q_H\): a vertical closed halfspace then contains the entire target fiber. These are all vertical cases of the first inequality in (1).

Now let \(\mathbf v\ne\mathbf0\), and let \(H^-\) be the opposite closed halfspace, obtained by replacing \(\ge t\) with \(\le t\). Put \(s_{\mathbf z}=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{\mathbf z}\cap H_{\mathbf z})\) and \(b_{\mathbf z}=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{\mathbf z}\cap H^-_{\mathbf z})\). For each fixed \(\mathbf z\), the common boundary is an affine hyperplane in \(\mathbb R^d\) with nonzero normal \(\mathbf v\). It has zero \(d\)-volume, so \(s_{\mathbf z}+b_{\mathbf z}=w_{\mathbf z}\) and \(b_{\mathbf j}=(1-p_{\mathbf j}(H))w_{\mathbf j}\). This is the boundary calculation of accepted fact \(\texttt{c13409b4041cc35d}\); it does not require the ambient boundary to pass through the target point.

If \(1-(1-p_{\mathbf j}(H))/\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)\le0\), the desired lower bound is trivial. Otherwise put \(\alpha=1-(1-p_{\mathbf j}(H))/\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)\), so \(0<\alpha\le1\), and form \(B=\{\mathbf z\in E:s_{\mathbf z}<\alpha w_{\mathbf z}\}\). For every \(\mathbf z\in B\), one has \(b_{\mathbf z}>(1-\alpha)w_{\mathbf z}\), so its complementary cap is nonempty and has positive volume. If \(\mathbf j\in\operatorname{conv}(B)\), take a barycentric representation with positive coefficients on a subset of \(B\). Applying (4) to the compact convex set \(C\cap H^-\) gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
b_{\mathbf j}^{1/d}
&\ge\sum_{\mathbf z\in B}\lambda_{\mathbf z}b_{\mathbf z}^{1/d}\\
&>(1-\alpha)^{1/d}
\sum_{\mathbf z\in B}\lambda_{\mathbf z}w_{\mathbf z}^{1/d}\\
&\ge\bigl((1-\alpha)\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)w_{\mathbf j}\bigr)^{1/d}\\
&=\bigl((1-p_{\mathbf j}(H))w_{\mathbf j}\bigr)^{1/d}
=b_{\mathbf j}^{1/d},
\end{aligned}
\]

a contradiction. Zero coefficients are omitted in applying (4). The strict inequality also holds when \(\alpha=1\), because every cap indexed by \(B\) then still has positive complementary volume, while its comparison term is zero. Thus \(\mathbf j\notin\operatorname{conv}(B)\).

Choose the base halfspace \(Q\ni\mathbf j\) avoiding \(B\) by finite separation, including the empty bad-set case. Summation gives \(\mu_C(H)\ge\sum_{\mathbf z\in E\cap Q}s_{\mathbf z}\ge\alpha\sum_{\mathbf z\in E\cap Q}w_{\mathbf z}\ge\alpha\tau_E(\mathbf j)\). This proves the first inequality of (1) for every proper closed ambient halfspace. If the full ambient space is included in the convention for closed halfspaces, its assertion is immediate from \(\tau_E(\mathbf j)\le W\).

If \(H\) contains \((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j})\), its nonvertical fiber section contains \(\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}\), so the Grünbaum input gives \(p_{\mathbf j}(H)\ge\gamma_d\). In the vertical case containing that point, \(p_{\mathbf j}(H)=1\), so the same inequality holds. Substitution into the first inequality of (1), followed by the infimum over all such containing halfspaces, proves its centroid conclusion. No halfspace is required to have boundary through the centroid in this deduction.

We next prove (2). Fix a convex majorant \(\varphi\), its weights \(q_{\mathbf z}\), an arbitrary \(\mathbf j\in D_+\), and any containing halfspace \(H\ni(\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j})\). For a vertical halfspace, its base halfspace \(Q_H\) contains \(\mathbf j\), and \(w_{\mathbf z}\ge q_{\mathbf z}\) gives \(\mu_C(H)\ge\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+\cap Q_H}q_{\mathbf z}\ge\tau_q(\mathbf j)\).

For a nonvertical halfspace, use the same compact complementary caps and the same \(s_{\mathbf z},b_{\mathbf z}\) as above. Grünbaum and the majorant hypothesis give \(b_{\mathbf j}\le\theta_dw_{\mathbf j}\le\theta_d\varphi(\mathbf j)^d\). Let \(B=\{\mathbf z\in D_+:s_{\mathbf z}<q_{\mathbf z}\}\). A point of \(B\) must have \(q_{\mathbf z}>0\); consequently \(b_{\mathbf z}=w_{\mathbf z}-s_{\mathbf z}>w_{\mathbf z}-q_{\mathbf z}=\theta_d\varphi(\mathbf z)^d>0\). If \(\mathbf j\in\operatorname{conv}(B)\), take positive barycentric coefficients on its representing points. Then (4) and convexity of \(\varphi\) imply

\[
\begin{aligned}
b_{\mathbf j}^{1/d}
&\ge\sum_{\mathbf z\in B}\lambda_{\mathbf z}b_{\mathbf z}^{1/d}\\
&>\theta_d^{1/d}\sum_{\mathbf z\in B}\lambda_{\mathbf z}\varphi(\mathbf z)\\
&\ge\theta_d^{1/d}\varphi(\mathbf j),
\end{aligned}
\]

contradicting the upper bound on \(b_{\mathbf j}\). Finite separation therefore supplies a proper closed \(Q\ni\mathbf j\) avoiding \(B\), and \(\mu_C(H)\ge\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+\cap Q}s_{\mathbf z}\ge\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+\cap Q}q_{\mathbf z}\ge\tau_q(\mathbf j)\). The empty bad-set case is included. Taking the infimum over all containing halfspaces proves the pointwise assertion in (2).

If \(Q_\varphi=0\), any \(\mathbf j\in D_+\) proves its existence assertion. Otherwise let \(E_q=\{\mathbf z\in D_+:q_{\mathbf z}>0\}\). Apply the weighted lattice centerpoint construction from accepted fact \(\texttt{bb2b5f9519ae23e8}\) to \(E_q\) with weights \(q_{\mathbf z}\). It yields \(\mathbf j_\varphi\in\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{conv}(E_q)\) with \(\tau_q(\mathbf j_\varphi)\ge2^{-n}Q_\varphi\). The positivity argument at the start of the proof shows \(\mathbf j_\varphi\in D_+\), so its actual fiber centroid is defined. Applying the pointwise inequality already proved gives (2). The weights and the selected point depend only on \(C\) and \(\varphi\), and are fixed before the containing halfspace is chosen. Taking the supremum over majorants proves the stated bound for \(h_{\max}(C)\).

For the aggregate error, nonnegativity and the definition of the positive part give

\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_\varphi
&\ge W-\theta_d\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+}\varphi(\mathbf z)^d\\
&=\gamma_d W-\theta_d\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+}
\bigl(\varphi(\mathbf z)^d-w_{\mathbf z}\bigr)\\
&\ge(\gamma_d-\theta_d\varepsilon)W.
\end{aligned}
\]

Combining this with \(Q_\varphi\ge0\) and (2) proves (3). Any affine majorant positive on \(D_+\) is positive throughout its convex hull, since an affine value at a convex combination is the same combination of its positive values. It is a convex majorant there, so this includes the stated affine-majorant certificate.

For the original comparison hypothesis, set \(\widehat\varphi=M_0^{1/d}\varphi\). This is a positive convex majorant. Since \(m_0\varphi(\mathbf z)^d\le w_{\mathbf z}\), its excess weights satisfy

\[
\begin{aligned}
\bigl(w_{\mathbf z}-\theta_d\widehat\varphi(\mathbf z)^d\bigr)_+
&\ge w_{\mathbf z}-\theta_dM_0\varphi(\mathbf z)^d\\
&\ge\left(1-\frac{M_0}{m_0}\theta_d\right)w_{\mathbf z}
=\beta w_{\mathbf z}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Taking marginal-depth infima preserves this inequality because \(\beta>0\). The pointwise assertion of (2) therefore gives \(h_C((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))\ge\beta\tau(\mathbf j)\) for every \(\mathbf j\in D_+\). Applying the accepted lattice centerpoint construction to \(D_+\) with the actual weights gives \(\mathbf j\in D_+\) with \(\tau(\mathbf j)\ge2^{-n}W\). This proves consequence 1, including its assertion for every such centerpoint. Notice that \(0<\beta\le\gamma_d<1\) follows from \(M_0/m_0\ge1\).

If \(w_{\mathbf z}=L(\mathbf z)^d\) with positive affine \(L\) on \(D_+\), it is positive and convex on the convex hull, and consequence 1 applies with \(\varphi=L\) and \(m_0=M_0=1\). If \(w_{\mathbf z}=e^{\ell(\mathbf z)}\), take \(\varphi=e^{\ell/d}\) and again \(m_0=M_0=1\). The latter function is positive and convex because the exponential has positive second derivative and its argument is affine. This proves the exact affine-root and log-affine claims of consequence 2.

For consequence 3, take \(\varphi=e^{\ell/d}\), \(m_0=\exp(\min_{D_+}(\log w-\ell))\), and \(M_0=\exp(\max_{D_+}(\log w-\ell))\). These finite extrema exist because \(D_+\) is finite and the volumes are positive. They give \(m_0\varphi(\mathbf z)^d\le w_{\mathbf z}\le M_0\varphi(\mathbf z)^d\) exactly, with \(M_0/m_0=e^\omega\). Thus consequence 1 yields the coefficient \(1-e^\omega\theta_d\) whenever positive. If \(\omega\le\varepsilon\) and \(\beta_\varepsilon>0\), this coefficient is at least \(\beta_\varepsilon\), proving the stated pointwise and centerpoint bounds. An absolute error at most \(\varepsilon\) puts the residual in \([-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\), so its oscillation is at most \(2\varepsilon\).

For the local affine lower support in consequence 4, every barycentric representation of \(\mathbf j\) from \(E\) gives \(\sum_{\mathbf z\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf z}w_{\mathbf z}^{1/d}\ge\sum_{\mathbf z\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf z}L(\mathbf z)=L(\mathbf j)>0\). Therefore \(\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)\ge L(\mathbf j)^d/w_{\mathbf j}\ge1/R\). The centroid inequality in (1) and monotonicity of \(t\mapsto[1-\theta_d/t]_+\) for \(t>0\) give the asserted bound. In the \(7/8\) to \(9/8\) comparison, one can apply consequence 1 directly with \(\varphi=L_0\), \(m_0=7/8\), and \(M_0=9/8\), obtaining \(\beta=1-(9/7)\theta_d=(9\gamma_d-2)/7\). Equivalently, the local bound uses \(L=(7/8)^{1/d}L_0\) and \(R=9/7\).

Finally, \(\log(1+1/d)<1/d\), as follows by integrating \((1+t)^{-1}<1\) for \(0<t\le1/d\). Hence \(\gamma_d=\exp(-d\log(1+1/d))>e^{-1}\). Also \(e=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}1/k!<2+\sum_{k=2}^{\infty}2^{-(k-1)}=3\), since \(k!\ge2^{k-1}\) and the inequality is strict for \(k\ge3\). It follows that \((9\gamma_d-2)/7>1/7\) and, at \(\varepsilon=1/4\), \(\gamma_d-\theta_d/4=(5\gamma_d-1)/4>(5-e)/(4e)>0\). Furthermore \(\beta_\varepsilon>1-e^\varepsilon(1-e^{-1})\), whose right-hand side is positive precisely when \(\varepsilon<\log(e/(e-1))\). These verify all the stated dimension-independent constants.
statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and set \(S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\). For \(\mathbf z\in\mathbb R^n\), write \(C_{\mathbf z}=\{\mathbf x:(\mathbf z,\mathbf x)\in C\}\) and \(w_{\mathbf z}=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{\mathbf z})\), with empty fibers having volume zero. Assume \(W=\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_{\mathbf z}>0\), and put \(D_+=\{\mathbf z\in\mathbb Z^n:w_{\mathbf z}>0\}\). This is a nonempty finite set. For \(\mathbf j\in D_+\), let \(\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}=w_{\mathbf j}^{-1}\int_{C_{\mathbf j}}\mathbf x\,d\mathbf x\) be the actual fiber centroid. Set \(\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d\) and \(\theta_d=1-\gamma_d\).

For an ambient closed halfspace \(H\), write \(H_{\mathbf z}=\{\mathbf x:(\mathbf z,\mathbf x)\in H\}\) and \(\mu_C(H)=\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\). For \(\mathbf y\in S\), the notation \(h_C(\mathbf y)\) means exactly the locked depth \(h_S(\mathbf y)=\inf_{H\ni\mathbf y}\mu_C(H)\). Also write \(h_{\max}(C)=\sup_{\mathbf y\in S}h_C(\mathbf y)\) and \((t)_+=\max\{t,0\}\).

The fiber notation agrees with accepted fact \(\texttt{bb2b5f9519ae23e8}\). In accepted fact \(\texttt{c13409b4041cc35d}\), the quantity \(a(z)\) is our \(w_{\mathbf z}\), and its complementary cap volume \(b(z)\) will be written \(b_{\mathbf z}\) when a halfspace is fixed. To avoid conflicts with predecessor cap-root and maximum-depth notation, the original comparison source's \(D,r,m,M\) are denoted here by \(D_+,\varphi,m_0,M_0\). The local-transfer source's \(\mathbf m,a_{\mathbf z},b_{\mathbf m}(a;E)\) become \(\mathbf j,w_{\mathbf z},\tau_E(\mathbf j)\), respectively.

For every nonempty \(E\subseteq D_+\) and \(\mathbf j\in\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{conv}(E)\), define

\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_E(\mathbf j)
&=\inf_{\substack{Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ proper closed halfspace}\\ \mathbf j\in Q}}
\sum_{\mathbf z\in E\cap Q}w_{\mathbf z},\\
\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)
&=\frac{1}{w_{\mathbf j}}
\min_{\substack{\lambda_{\mathbf z}\ge0\ (\mathbf z\in E),\ \sum_{\mathbf z\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf z}=1\\
\sum_{\mathbf z\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf z}\mathbf z=\mathbf j}}
\left(\sum_{\mathbf z\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf z}w_{\mathbf z}^{1/d}\right)^d.
\end{aligned}
\]

The target fiber has \(w_{\mathbf j}>0\), the displayed minimum is attained, and \(0<\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)\le1\). Put \(\tau(\mathbf j)=\tau_{D_+}(\mathbf j)\). For every closed ambient halfspace \(H\), including those that do not contain the target fiber centroid, let \(p_{\mathbf j}(H)=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{\mathbf j}\cap H_{\mathbf j})/w_{\mathbf j}\). Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_C(H)
&\ge\tau_E(\mathbf j)
\left[1-\frac{1-p_{\mathbf j}(H)}{\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)}\right]_+,\\
h_C((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))
&\ge\tau_E(\mathbf j)
\left[1-\frac{\theta_d}{\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)}\right]_+.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]

There is also the following certificate without a single multiplicative comparison constant. Let \(\varphi:\operatorname{conv}(D_+)\to(0,\infty)\) be convex and satisfy \(\varphi(\mathbf z)^d\ge w_{\mathbf z}\) for every \(\mathbf z\in D_+\). Define the fixed weights \(q_{\mathbf z}=(w_{\mathbf z}-\theta_d\varphi(\mathbf z)^d)_+\), their total \(Q_\varphi=\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+}q_{\mathbf z}\), and their marginal depth \(\tau_q(\mathbf j)=\inf_{Q\ni\mathbf j}\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+\cap Q}q_{\mathbf z}\), with the same proper closed base halfspaces as above. The first inequality below holds for every \(\mathbf j\in D_+\), and there exists \(\mathbf j_\varphi\in D_+\) satisfying the second:

\[
\begin{aligned}
h_C((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))
&\ge\tau_q(\mathbf j)\qquad(\mathbf j\in D_+),\\
h_C((\mathbf j_\varphi,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j_\varphi}))
&\ge2^{-n}Q_\varphi.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]

In particular, \(h_{\max}(C)\ge2^{-n}\sup_\varphi Q_\varphi\), where the supremum is over these positive convex majorants. This class is nonempty, since a sufficiently large positive constant is a majorant. If such a majorant satisfies \(\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+}(\varphi(\mathbf z)^d-w_{\mathbf z})\le\varepsilon W\) for some \(\varepsilon\ge0\), then

\[
h_{\max}(C)\ge[\gamma_d-\theta_d\varepsilon]_+\,2^{-n}W.
\tag{3}
\]

Thus an aggregate majorant error at most \(W/4\) gives \(h_{\max}(C)\ge(5-e)(4e)^{-1}2^{-n}W\). Taking \(\varphi=L\) for an affine majorant gives exactly the affine-majorant excess \(Q_L=\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+}(w_{\mathbf z}-\theta_dL(\mathbf z)^d)_+\).

The following profile consequences also hold.

1. Suppose a positive convex reference \(\varphi\) on \(\operatorname{conv}(D_+)\) and constants \(0<m_0\le M_0\) satisfy \(m_0\varphi(\mathbf z)^d\le w_{\mathbf z}\le M_0\varphi(\mathbf z)^d\) for all \(\mathbf z\in D_+\). If \(\beta=1-(M_0/m_0)\theta_d>0\), then \(h_C((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))\ge\beta\tau(\mathbf j)\) for every \(\mathbf j\in D_+\). There exists \(\mathbf j\in D_+\) with \(\tau(\mathbf j)\ge2^{-n}W\), and every such \(\mathbf j\) satisfies \(h_C((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))\ge\beta2^{-n}W\). This is the original coefficient \(\beta=1-(M/m)(1-\gamma_d)\) under the alias map above.

2. If \(w_{\mathbf z}=L(\mathbf z)^d\) on \(D_+\), where \(L\) is affine and positive on \(D_+\), then the first consequence holds with \(\beta=\gamma_d\). The same conclusion holds if \(w_{\mathbf z}=e^{\ell(\mathbf z)}\) on \(D_+\) for an affine \(\ell\). In either case, \(h_C((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))\ge\gamma_d\tau(\mathbf j)\) for every positive integer fiber, and every weighted lattice centerpoint of the actual weights has depth at least \(\gamma_d2^{-n}W>e^{-1}2^{-n}W\).

3. More generally, let \(\ell\) be affine and put \(\omega=\operatorname{osc}_{D_+}(\log w-\ell)\), where oscillation means the maximum minus the minimum of \(\log w_{\mathbf z}-\ell(\mathbf z)\) over \(D_+\). The exact comparison coefficient is \(1-e^\omega\theta_d\). If \(\omega\le\varepsilon\) and \(\beta_\varepsilon=1-e^\varepsilon\theta_d>0\), then \(h_C((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))\ge\beta_\varepsilon\tau(\mathbf j)\) for every \(\mathbf j\in D_+\). At a weighted lattice centerpoint this gives \(h_C((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))\ge\beta_\varepsilon2^{-n}W\). In particular, a fixed \(0\le\varepsilon<\log(e/(e-1))\) gives the positive dimension-independent lower coefficient \(1-e^\varepsilon(1-e^{-1})\). If instead the hypothesis is the absolute error \(|\log w_{\mathbf z}-\ell(\mathbf z)|\le\varepsilon\), the corresponding oscillation bound is \(2\varepsilon\), so the coefficient is \(1-e^{2\varepsilon}\theta_d\) whenever positive.

4. In the local setting of (1), suppose an affine \(L\), positive on \(E\), satisfies \(L(\mathbf z)^d\le w_{\mathbf z}\) on \(E\) and \(w_{\mathbf j}\le R L(\mathbf j)^d\) for a scalar \(R\ge1\). Then \(h_C((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))\ge[1-R\theta_d]_+\tau_E(\mathbf j)\). In particular, if an affine \(L_0>0\) on \(D_+\) satisfies \((7/8)L_0(\mathbf z)^d\le w_{\mathbf z}\le(9/8)L_0(\mathbf z)^d\) throughout \(D_+\), then every weighted lattice centerpoint of the actual weights has depth at least \((9\gamma_d-2)7^{-1}2^{-n}W>W/(7\cdot2^n)\).
